title: Refrain reference-protocol meta tags
description: The shared, versioned contract for the `meta` tags that organize the protocol library. Refrain itself is meta-agnostic; host apps read these tags (via refrain.read_meta) to group/filter/search. Unknown fields are permitted and ignored; unknown enum values fall into an 'Other' bucket rather than being dropped.

description.description: One-line human label shown in the picker.

title.description: Plain-language, goal-first name shown as the primary label (e.g. 'Calm the mind — boost alpha').

summary.description: One non-specialist sentence describing what the protocol trains.

family.description: Shared id across a concept's variant files; the picker groups by it.

feedback_asset_bundle.description: Optional host-approved bundled audio set for a layered-texture protocol. A host may reject unknown bundle names.

status.description: OUR file maturity / test status (distinct from `evidence`, which describes the technique's prior art). 'legacy' marks a protocol superseded by a newer one: still runnable, hidden from the default picker.

evidence.description: How established the signal-training APPROACH is in prior art (distinct from `status`, which is our file's maturity). This is provenance about the technique, not a claim about outcomes for any person.

citation.description: Author-anchored reference for where the approach comes from — origin and prior art, not proof of outcome. Required once status > draft.

goals.description: Wellness-framed training goal categories (MULTI-membership). Drives the picker's groups. Controlled vocab; a host app buckets an unknown value into 'Other' rather than dropping the protocol. These are training goals, not indications: no diagnostic or therapeutic claim is made or implied.

bands.description: Band chips shown on the row. Modality-scoped and optional: EEG bands like 'alpha'/'smr', HRV bands like 'hrv-lf'. Omit for modalities with no band concept, e.g. a raw skin-conductance level.

site.description: Channel / source label — an EEG scalp site such as 'Cz' or 'F3/F4', or a non-EEG source label such as 'tachogram', 'gsr', 'temp'.

threshold_style.description: Drives the Adaptive / Baseline filter chip. 'selectable' = the protocol exposes a `mode` control offering both.

hardware.description: Capability class the protocol targets. 'research_amp' = greyed out on a consumer device.

requires_features.description: Engine/hardware features the protocol needs (e.g. dc_coupling, trials). Used to grey-out unrunnable protocols.
